A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MAPKAP kinase-2 (MK-2) plays a crucial role in the regulation and severity of the systemic inflammatory response in acute pancreatitis.

the homozygotic deletion of the MK-2 gene ameliorated the severity of acute pancreatic inflammation, and attenuated the systemic inflammatory reactions, and the increased expression of HSP 25 and 60 after induction of AP, and the increased HSP 60 after Cer+LSP treatment, in both wild-type and MK2-/-mice.
MK2 seems to play an important role in the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of acute pancreatitis, which may be due to its effects on the regulation of cytokine production.
